How ProofCheck Works

Technical overview and user guide for the ProofCheck platform.

Contents

Overview Architecture User Flow Result Statuses Evidence & Verification Rebuttal System Technical Details FAQ

Overview

ProofCheck is a decentralized application for verifying public claims about GitHub repositories. Instead of simply trusting a claim, ProofCheck creates an immutable record of the evidence, the verification process, and the validator consensus.

Key Features

📝 Public Claims

Submit verifiable statements about GitHub repositories.

🔐 Evidence Fingerprinting

SHA-256 hashes capture content at the moment of review.

🗳️ Validator Consensus

GenLayer validators independently verify and reach consensus.

⛓️ On-Chain Record

All results stored immutably on GenLayer blockchain.

💬 Rebuttals

Challenge results with counter-evidence without deleting history.

📊 Review Trail

Complete history of all reviews remains visible.

Architecture

ProofCheck operates as a decentralized system across three layers:

1. Frontend Layer

User interface for submitting claims, viewing results, and creating rebuttals. Built with vanilla JavaScript, HTML, and CSS.

2. Smart Contract Layer

Intelligent contract deployed on GenLayer that receives claims and triggers validator consensus.

Contract: ProofCheck v1.1.0 Network: GenLayer Studio Next (chainId: 61997) Address: 0x32761911D56A00BcB5893D57e290e73243FdFd79

3. Blockchain Layer

GenLayer blockchain provides validator consensus, on-chain storage, and immutability guarantees.

User Flow

Submitting a Claim

Submit Claim
User fills form with claim type, statement, repository URL, and evidence URLs.
Attach Evidence
User supplies public evidence URLs for validators to inspect during consensus.
Connect Wallet
User connects MetaMask wallet for transaction signing.
Estimate Network Fee
The dApp requests the current GenLayer network fee estimate before signing.
Submit for Free
The verification fee is 0 GEN on testnet; a separate network fee may still apply.
Consensus
GenLayer validators independently verify and reach consensus on verdict.
On-Chain Storage
Claim, submitter, evidence URLs, status, and validator reason are stored on-chain.
Display Result
Frontend reads result from blockchain and displays to user.

Result Statuses

Each claim receives one of three verdicts from validator consensus:

Status Meaning Example
✅ SUPPORTED Public evidence fits the wording of the claim at review time. Repository is public, contains relevant code, and has MIT License.
⚠️ INSUFFICIENT Sources are missing, inaccessible, ambiguous, or not specific enough. Repository found but license requirements unclear or conflicting.
❌ REFUTED Evidence directly contradicts the wording of the claim. Repository is private or licensed under proprietary terms.

Evidence & Verification

Evidence Capture

When you submit a claim, ProofCheck stores:

  • URL: Direct link to the evidence source
  • Claim: The statement and selected claim type
  • Submitter: The connected wallet address
  • Result: Status and validator explanation after consensus

Validator Verification

GenLayer validators independently:

  1. Fetch each evidence URL
  2. Compare content with the claim statement
  3. Assess whether evidence supports, contradicts, or is insufficient for the claim
  4. Vote on the verdict

Consensus Decision

The majority vote among validators becomes the on-chain verdict. This ensures no single validator controls the outcome.

Rebuttal System

ProofCheck allows anyone to challenge a result by submitting counter-evidence:

How Rebuttals Work

  1. View a claim detail page
  2. Scroll to "Rebuttal" section
  3. Provide a counter-evidence URL (different evidence that contradicts the current result)
  4. Explain what should be revisited
  5. Submit a new claim with the counter-evidence
  6. New review is added as a separate claim
  7. Original claim remains visible (never deleted)

No Deletion of History

When a rebuttal is successful, the new verdict is added to the review history—the old verdict isn't removed. This creates a transparent audit trail showing how consensus changed over time.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who decides the verdict?

GenLayer validators reach consensus through independent verification. No single person or organization controls the outcome.

Can the verdict be changed?

Yes, through rebuttals. New evidence can lead to new reviews, which may change the consensus. All historical verdicts remain visible.

Is this a permanent certification?

No. ProofCheck records a snapshot of evidence at a specific moment in time. Repositories change, licenses change—the claim remains true only for the evidence that was verified.

What if validators disagree?

Majority vote wins. Dissenting validators' opinions are recorded on-chain for transparency.

Why might my wallet show a fee?

ProofCheck charges 0 GEN for verification on testnet. GenLayer may still require a separate network or consensus fee to process the transaction.

Can I challenge a verdict?

Rebuttal submissions are planned for a later step. For now, each claim keeps its own transparent result and evidence trail.

How long does verification take?

Consensus typically takes 1-2 blocks (~1-2 minutes on GenLayer). Results are visible immediately in the UI once consensus is reached.

What claim types are supported?

Currently MVP supports: "Repository is open source" and "Repository has a usable license". More claim types coming in future versions.
